I expanded the 4B record with more independent corroboration and cleaner source splits on election suppression, protest treatment, media control, and institutional capture. I still could not update `research-ledger-manifest.json` because the workspace is read-only.

**What changed**
- I added stronger independent sources for the 2023 authoritarian record:
  - Freedom House 2024 country report for elections, loyalist appointments, and the revised Counterespionage Law.
  - Amnesty’s 2023 protest and censorship coverage, especially White Paper protests and protest aftereffects.
  - CECC’s 2023 annual report for political prisoners, protest repression, and technology-enabled authoritarianism.
  - RSF materials for press repression and detention of journalists.
- I tightened the chapter’s factual spine:
  - No competitive national elections.
  - Systematic blocking of independent candidates and opposition.
  - Expanded surveillance and censorship.
  - Continued detention and punishment of protesters, lawyers, journalists, and activists.
  - No meaningful independent institutions capable of constraining Xi.

**Best-supported chapter conclusions**
- `4B.1` remains strongly adverse: there was no genuine national electoral contestation.
- `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.6`, and `4B.9` are all strongly adverse: criticism, oversight, media, and digital freedom were tightly controlled.
- `4B.5` is adverse: appointments and institution-building continued to favor loyalty and political conformity.
- `4B.10` is adverse: the period did not strengthen democratic resilience; it reinforced authoritarian rule.

**Useful new source links**
- Freedom House 2024 China report: https://freedomhouse.org/country/china/freedom-world/2024
- Amnesty on protest history and White Paper movement:
  - https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2023/06/right-to-peaceful-protest-in-china-on-tiananmen-anniversary/
  - https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/campaigns/2023/11/chinas-white-paper-movement-one-year-on-six-protesters-share-their-stories/
- Amnesty China reporting hub: https://www.amnesty.org/en/location/asia-and-the-pacific/east-asia/china/report-china/
- RSF China press-freedom profile: https://rsf.org/en/country/china
- CECC 2023 annual report: https://www.cecc.gov/publications/annual-reports/2023-annual-report

**Remaining gaps**
- I still do not have a clean, case-level dataset showing remedies or institutional resistance inside China.
- The chapter remains heavily reliant on monitor/reporting sources because China suppresses open complaint volume and independent scrutiny.
